intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Huawei found guilty on 10 of 12 US counts
items.text: A jury in New York has convicted the Chinese technology company Huawei on 10 of 12 criminal counts. The charges included bank fraud, wire fraud, breaking sanctions and a conspiracy to steal trade secrets. The jury cleared the company of two other counts, obstruction conspiracy and racketeering conspiracy. The trial lasted about two months and was linked to the firm's business in Iran. A judge will pass sentence in September 2027. Huawei has long denied wrongdoing, and the result is likely to raise tension between Washington and Beijing.

gloss.convict: to decide in court that someone is guilty of a crime
gloss.count: one separate charge in a criminal case
gloss.sanctions: official penalties that stop trade with a country
gloss.conspiracy: a secret plan by several people to do something illegal
gloss.clear of: to decide officially that someone is not guilty of
gloss.pass sentence: for a judge to announce a punishment

items.title: Houthis hit Riyadh tower for second time
items.text: Yemen's Houthi group has attacked the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund in Riyadh for the second time in less than a week. The building stands in the King Abdullah Financial District and is the tallest tower in the Saudi capital. Eleven people were injured in the latest strike. A Saudi-led coalition condemned the incident as a terrorist attack. The Houthis have not yet explained how the weapon got past the city's air defences. The strikes come while the region is already tense after weeks of fighting around the Gulf.

gloss.headquarters: the main office of an organisation
gloss.coalition: a group of countries or groups that work together
gloss.condemn: to say publicly that something is very bad or wrong
gloss.strike: a military attack, often from the air
gloss.air defences: systems that protect a place from attack by aircraft or missiles
gloss.tense: nervous and likely to turn into conflict

items.title: Capita chief resigns over pensions problems
items.text: The chief executive of the British outsourcing firm Capita, Adolfo Hernandez, has resigned with immediate effect. The company has had problems running the Civil Service Pension Scheme, which has about 1.7 million members. Capita is also raising £190m of new capital. Its share price has fallen by roughly 70 per cent to 72p. Separately, a new survey showed that UK business activity grew for the fifth month in a row in November, although hiring has weakened and services lagged behind factories.

gloss.outsourcing: paying another company to do work for you
gloss.raise capital: to collect money for a company from investors
gloss.share price: the cost of one part of a company on the stock market
gloss.in a row: one after another without a break

items.title: Real Madrid beat PSV 5-1 in Champions League
items.text: Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday night. The Dutch side took the lead from a penalty by Ivan Perisic in the 32nd minute. Federico Valverde then equalised, and Jude Bellingham put the hosts ahead. Kylian Mbappe scored twice and Vinicius Junior added another goal to complete the win. The result was a strong response from the Spanish club after the early setback. PSV are managed by Jose Mourinho.

gloss.take the lead: to go ahead in a game
gloss.equalise: to score a goal that makes the score level
gloss.penalty: a free shot at goal after a foul in the box

items.title: Man City draw 2-2 with Napoli at the Etihad
items.text: Manchester City and Napoli drew 2-2 at the Etihad Stadium in the Champions League on Tuesday. Napoli scored twice through Rasmus Hojlund and Noah Lang, but City fought back to share the points. The game was also the first time Kevin De Bruyne had returned to Manchester as an opponent. The Belgian midfielder spent ten years at City before leaving the club. The draw leaves both teams with work to do in the league phase table. In another match, Galatasaray beat Aston Villa with a late goal.

gloss.draw: a game that ends with the same score for both teams
gloss.fight back: to start playing better after losing
gloss.opponent: a person or team you play against
gloss.midfielder: a football player who plays in the middle of the pitch
gloss.league phase: the first stage of the competition where all teams play each other

items.title: Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang as chief executive
items.text: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, less than two weeks after he resigned. The decision was announced on Monday. Shares in the chip maker jumped, and US stocks rose sharply as investors welcomed the news. Huang is due to appear before Congress next week. The US attorney general, Todd Blanche, called Nvidia a good corporate citizen but would not say whether the company or its boss is under federal investigation. The firm has not explained in detail why Huang stepped down.

gloss.reinstate: to give someone their old job or position back
gloss.resign: to leave a job by your own choice
gloss.shares: small parts of a company that people can buy
gloss.federal: relating to the national government of the US
gloss.investor: a person who puts money into a company to make a profit

items.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to Tiangong
items.text: China has launched the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft from the Jiuquan centre in the Gobi Desert. On board are two Chinese astronauts and Muhammad Zeeshan Ali from Pakistan. He is the first foreign astronaut to fly to China's Tiangong space station. The mission shows how Beijing wants to work with other countries in space while it builds its own programme. The crew will spend several months on the station, carrying out experiments before they return to Earth.

gloss.launch: to send a rocket or spacecraft into the air
gloss.on board: inside a ship, plane or spacecraft
gloss.space station: a large spacecraft where people live and work in orbit
gloss.programme: a planned set of activities with a goal
gloss.experiment: a scientific test to find out something

items.title: BIFA announces its craft award winners
items.text: The British Independent Film Awards has named the winners of its craft categories. I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, directed by Clio Barnard, won three awards, for casting, editing and music supervision. Savage House took two, for make-up and hair, and for costume design. Other winners included A Long Winter for cinematography and Rose of Nevada for sound. The remaining categories will be revealed at a ceremony at the Roundhouse in London on Sunday 6 December.

gloss.craft award: a prize for technical skills in film, such as editing or costumes
gloss.cinematography: the art of filming and lighting a movie
gloss.reveal: to show or tell something that was secret
gloss.ceremony: a formal event to give out prizes

items.title: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in $44bn deal
items.text: The cyber security firm CrowdStrike has agreed to buy its rival Zscaler in an all-share deal worth about $44bn. Under the plan, Zscaler's owners will be paid in CrowdStrike shares rather than cash. Investors reacted in different ways. Shares in CrowdStrike fell by about nine per cent, while Zscaler's rose by around 18 per cent. If it goes ahead, the takeover would be one of the biggest deals in the technology sector this year.

gloss.cyber security: the protection of computers and data from attack
gloss.all-share deal: a purchase paid for with shares instead of cash
gloss.rival: a person or company that competes with another
gloss.takeover: when one company buys control of another

items.title: GTA VI sets record with $3.79bn on day one
items.text: Rockstar Games has said that Grand Theft Auto VI made $3.79bn in retail sales on its first day. The company called it a record and said the figure covered launch day, Thursday 19 November. It also said that 32.5 million copies were sold before release, another record across all platforms. For comparison, GTA V took three days to earn $1bn in 2013. The standard edition costs around $80 in the US. Studio co-founder Sam Houser said the team was humbled by the response.

gloss.retail sales: money from selling products to customers
gloss.launch day: the first day a product is on sale
gloss.pre-release: before something is officially on sale
gloss.for comparison: to show the difference with something else
